healthcareSystem: Mixed public-private system. Public healthcare is free but severely under-resourced. Private hospitals in Lusaka and Livingstone offer better care. English is the official language, which helps with medical communication.
qualityNotes: Private hospitals in Lusaka provide reasonable care for common conditions. Public hospitals are overcrowded and under-equipped. Healthcare quality outside major cities is very limited. Serious conditions may require evacuation to South Africa.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in cities open 8am-6pm weekdays, 8am-1pm Saturdays. Some supermarket pharmacies have extended hours. Limited availability in rural areas.
pharmacyTips: Buy from registered pharmacies only — look for the Pharmacy Board registration. Shoprite and Pick n Pay supermarkets have pharmacy sections in Lusaka. Pharmacists speak English. Avoid purchasing medications from informal markets.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is inconsistent. Many medications available without prescription at pharmacies. Antibiotics and antimalarials readily available OTC. Purchase only from licensed pharmacies.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly illegal. Severe penalties including imprisonment.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances require documentation. Carry a doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry original packaging and prescription documentation.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications. English is the official language so English documentation is accepted. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring sufficient supply for your trip.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is essential. Serious conditions may require evacuation to Johannesburg, South Africa. Ensure coverage includes malaria treatment and adventure activities if visiting Victoria Falls.

required: Yellow Fever (required if arriving from an endemic country; recommended for all travelers)
recommended: Malaria prophylaxis (essential — malaria is endemic throughout Zambia)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow Fever vaccination certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Malaria prophylaxis is strongly recommended — Zambia has high malaria transmission, especially during the rainy season (November-April).

waterNotes: Tap water is NOT safe to drink. Use bottled water for drinking and brushing teeth. Avoid ice in drinks outside of international hotels and lodges. Bottled water is widely available in cities and tourist areas.
foodSafetyTips: Eat at established restaurants and safari lodges. Avoid raw vegetables and unpeeled fruits from street vendors. Nshima (cornmeal staple) is generally safe when freshly prepared. Safari lodges maintain high food safety standards. Wash hands frequently.
medicalTourismNote: Zambia is not a medical tourism destination. Private hospitals in Lusaka serve the local and expat community.
metaDescription: Health guide for Zambia: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, bottled water only, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Medland Hospital
hospitals.notes: Private hospital with good facilities. English-speaking staff. Popular with expats and tourists.

hospitals.name: Fairview Hospital
hospitals.notes: Well-regarded private hospital. Good emergency department. English-speaking.

hospitals.name: Livingstone General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital near Victoria Falls. Basic but accessible. For serious cases, evacuation to Lusaka or South Africa may be needed.

hospitals.name: SES Clinic Livingstone
hospitals.notes: Private clinic in Livingstone specializing in emergency and travel medicine. Good first point of contact near Victoria Falls.

pharmacyPhrases.local: I need headache medicine (English is official language)

dentalCare.availability: Limited but available in Lusaka. Private dental clinics offer reasonable care.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care in Lusaka is adequate for basic procedures. English-speaking dentists available. Very limited outside major cities.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies near Victoria Falls, you may need to travel to Lusaka or cross to Livingstone, Zimbabwe for more options.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Limited availability in Lusaka through private practices and expat networks.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are limited but improving. English-speaking counselors available in Lusaka. Telehealth from your home country is recommended for ongoing mental health support.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited throughout Zambia.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Private hospitals in Lusaka have basic wheelchair access. Public hospitals may not.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Private vehicles or adapted safari vehicles are the best option.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Safari lodges increasingly offer accessible options. Contact accommodations in advance. Victoria Falls area has some accessible viewing points. Bring all assistive devices.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at private clinics and Lusaka hospital facilities.
covidStatus.notes: COVID restrictions have been fully lifted. Standard precautions recommended.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private hospitals can provide English-language invoices. Pay out of pocket and submit for reimbursement. Some private facilities may assist with insurance pre-authorization. Keep all receipts and medical records.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private facilities. Public hospitals are cheaper but less well-equipped. Payment in Zambian kwacha or sometimes USD.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation to South Africa is the standard route for serious conditions. SES (Specialty Emergency Services) in Livingstone can coordinate evacuations for Victoria Falls area emergencies.
